subject: Banking
title: The Big Three Bureaus
description: A quick, practical guide to The Big Three Bureaus.

hook.text: Three companies hold the financial data of 220 million Americans: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion.

buildup.text: Credit bureaus collect data from banks, lenders, and public records.

discovery.text: You are the product, not the customer. Bureaus sell your data to lenders, employers, landlords, and insurance companies.

twist.text: Each bureau's file can differ because lenders do not report everywhere and errors do not spread evenly.

climax.text: Three private companies control America's credit system.

punchline.text: 220 million files. Three companies. You didn't sign up. They track you anyway.

quiz.question: Why can credit scores differ between bureaus?
options: Not all lenders report to all three bureaus

details.summary: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion are the three major credit bureaus that collect financial data on over 200 million Americans, selling credit reports and scores to lenders who use them to make billions of dollars in lending decisions daily.
details.whyItMatters: These three private companies effectively control access to credit for hundreds of millions of people. Their data accuracy, security practices, and business models directly impact who can borrow money and at what cost.
takeaways: Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion dominate credit reporting
Each bureau may have slightly different data on you
Bureaus profit from selling your data to lenders and marketing firms

faq.question: Why are there three bureaus instead of one?
faq.answer: The three bureaus developed independently as private businesses. There is no law mandating a single system. Each has different relationships with data furnishers, so your reports may differ across bureaus depending on which creditors report to which.

faq.question: How do credit bureaus make money?
faq.answer: Primarily by selling your credit data. Lenders pay to pull your report when you apply for credit. Bureaus also sell data to employers, landlords, insurance companies, and marketers. Your financial data is a product they sell for profit.
